metadata.core_objective: Teach financial autonomy by separating basic family contributions from earned money and using financial restitution as a real-world consequence.

topics.title: Citizenship Duties vs. Earned Commissions
topics.summary: Differentiating baseline household responsibilities from earned financial tasks.
key_principles: Citizenship duties are unpaid expectations required for living in a shared home.
Commissions are optional, value-add tasks that compensate effort and labor.

topics.title: Financial Restitution & Money Management
topics.summary: Using financial repair for property damage and instilling the 3-bucket money allocation model.

activities.title: Citizen vs. Commission Audit
activities.instructions: Categorize household chores into unpaid expectations versus paid commission jobs.

tasks.title: Household Bank & Restitution System Setup
tasks.action: Publish baseline expectations, extra commission opportunities, and financial debt repair labor rates.

quiz.question: Why is it problematic to pay children an allowance for basic self-care tasks like making their bed or picking up their toys?
options: A) It costs parents too much money.
B) It teaches children that basic household participation is optional if they decide they don't need the money.
C) Children do not understand monetary value until age 16.
D) It takes too long to track daily payouts.

quiz.question: What is the proper implementation of 'Financial Restitution' when a teenager accidentally breaks a household item during careless horseplay?
options: A) Grounding them for a month without addressing the broken item.
B) Forgiving the incident completely and paying for the replacement yourself without discussion.
C) Calculating the replacement/repair cost and allowing the teenager to pay from savings or work off the cost through extra commission tasks.
D) Yelling at them until they feel remorseful.
